posts.title: A CSCS logo is not a scaffold design — competence cards do not replace the TWC
posts.excerpt: Construction News, 25 September 2026, and ScaffMag, 28 September 2026: CISRS has given notice that it will leave the CSCS card scheme on 1 June 2027, citing legal advice on Construction Leadership Council card rules and work outside construction. CSCS disputes that reading and says the notice was unexpected. CISRS says existing cards remain valid for their five-year term and that qualifications will not change. For contractors the lesson is procedural: site access cards evidence training, not that the scaffold is designed, inspected or permitted under BS 5975-1:2024.
posts.linkedinReady:
A CISRS or CSCS card is evidence of training. It is not a design, not an inspection and not a permit to use the scaffold.

On 25 September 2026 Construction News reported that CISRS has given notice it will leave the CSCS scheme on 1 June 2027. CISRS cites legal advice on Construction Leadership Council card rules and the fact that a large share of scaffolding work sits outside construction. CSCS Group chief executive Sean Kearns has called the notice unexpected and does not accept that the CLC wording creates an immediate conflict. ScaffMag on 28 September set out both positions. CISRS says existing cards remain valid for their full term and that qualifications will not change. The exit can still be withdrawn if CLC wording is agreed.

For the TWC and TWS the control point does not move. CDM 2015 still requires competent people. BS 5975-1:2024 still requires the scaffold on the register, a brief when it is not a TG20:21 compliance sheet, inspection and a permit before load or public interface. Do not treat a gate-pass logo as proof the ties, sheeting, public protection or loadings have been checked.

body.p: Construction News reported on 25 September 2026 that the Construction Industry Scaffolders Record Scheme (CISRS) has given notice that it will withdraw from the Construction Skills Certification Scheme (CSCS) on 1 June 2027. CISRS, overseen by the National Access and Scaffolding Confederation, said legal advice found it at risk of breaching Construction Leadership Council industry card scheme rules that cards will not be issued for non-construction-related occupations. CISRS chief executive Clive Dickin said research showed between 30 and 80 per cent of scaffolding contractors' work is outside construction. From 1 January 2027 CISRS intends to rename itself the Competence in Scaffolding Record Scheme. It says qualifications, training routes and existing five-year cards will not change. New and renewed cards from June 2027 would be issued without the CSCS logo if the licence ends. CSCS group chief executive Sean Kearns described the notice as unexpected, said CSCS had been waiting for an update on outstanding licence obligations, and rejected the reading that CLC wording forces CISRS out. ScaffMag on 28 September 2026 reported CSCS confirming formal notice with a proposed termination date of 31 May 2027, and CISRS saying the exit can still be reversed if CLC Clause 4 is amended so one card can cover construction and other sectors.

Scaffolding is temporary works. The card debate is about how competence is recorded across construction, utilities, petrochemical, marine and aviation. It is not a change to TG20:21, EN 12811-1, Work at Height Regulations or BS 5975-1:2024. Principal contractors still have to satisfy themselves that the people erecting, altering and inspecting scaffolds are competent for the actual task. The TWC still has to put the scaffold on the register, decide whether it is a standard solution or needs a design brief, and hold inspection and permit-to-use before the public or the follow-on trade walks underneath. A logo on a card does not confirm ties into the facade, sheeting wind loads, TG20 compliance sheets, or that last week's alteration was inspected. CDM 2015 competence duties do not wait for 2027.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Treat CISRS/CSCS cards as one input to competence — not as design acceptance or a permit to use.
Keep scaffolds, sheeting, fans, loading bays and public-interface lifts on the temporary works register.
If the scaffold is not a documented TG20:21 compliance sheet for the actual geometry and wind, issue a design brief.
Do not load, sheet or hand over until the competent person has inspected and the project procedure has issued the permit.
Record who erected and who inspected. A gate-pass scan is not that record.

If your induction or procurement text currently says 'CSCS-logoed CISRS card only', plan how you will word competence after June 2027 — and keep the current wording under review during the notice period.
Provisional category only — confirm under the project temporary works procedure. Public interface, sheeting and unusual geometry push the category up.
Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

posts.title: A near-miss that is not closed out is still a public-protection temporary works risk
posts.excerpt: HSE Media Centre, 24 September 2026: St James Limited and Lindner Prater Limited were sentenced at Inner London Crown Court after Mick Ferris, 53, was killed on 2 October 2018 by a 130 kg window unit that fell about 300 feet from the 26th floor of the Corniche development on Albert Embankment. A window had already fallen from the same penthouses in August 2017 during construction and nearly hit two workers. The court found both companies guilty of breaching Section 3(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. Combined fines £1.3 million plus costs.
posts.linkedinReady:
A window that can fall onto a public footway is a falling-object risk to people who never signed onto the site.

On 24 September 2026 Inner London Crown Court sentenced St James Limited and Lindner Prater Limited after Mick Ferris, 53, was killed on 2 October 2018 by a 130 kg window unit that fell about 300 feet from the 26th floor of the Corniche on Albert Embankment. After a five-week trial both companies were found guilty of breaching Section 3(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. St James was fined £1 million plus £125,000 costs. Lindner Prater was fined £300,000 plus £125,000 costs.

HSE said the windows were changed from inward to outward opening and were never effectively risk assessed. Safety relied on a single restrictor held by a single screw. In August 2017 a window left open in the wind fell from the same penthouses during construction and nearly hit two workers. HSE said the review was not followed up effectively. Wind speeds were not unusually high on either occasion.

Register public falling-object risk. A near-miss is a hold point. Close the brief, the restraint and the inspection before the public walks underneath.

body.p: On 24 September 2026 HSE published the sentencing outcome after a five-week trial. Mick Ferris, 53, a coach driver and grandfather, was killed at about 10.30am on 2 October 2018 when a window unit weighing 130 kg fell about 300 feet from the 26th floor of the Corniche luxury development on Albert Embankment, London. He was on a break and returning to his coach. St James Group Limited, part of the Berkeley Group, was the developer, Principal Contractor and Principal Designer. Lindner Prater Limited was engaged by St James to design the penthouse windows. Both companies were found guilty of contravening Section 3(1) of the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974. At Inner London Crown Court, St James was fined £1 million and ordered to pay £125,000 costs. Lindner Prater Limited was fined £300,000 and ordered to pay £125,000 costs.

HSE reported that early in design the windows were changed from opening inwards to opening outwards, so that if they detached they would fall onto a pedestrian area, and that they were never effectively risk assessed. The safety of the windows relied on the performance of a single restrictor held in by a single screw. None of the fittings had been confirmed by their manufacturers as suitable for the bespoke curved penthouse windows. In August 2017, more than a year before the fatal incident, a window left open in windy conditions fell from the same penthouses during construction and nearly hit two workers. St James led an internal review. Records obtained by HSE showed key noted areas of concern were not followed up effectively. It was only after Mr Ferris death that the windows were redesigned to open inward. HSE lead inspector Andrew Verrall-Withers said both times a window fell the wind speeds were not unusually high, and that too much reliance was placed on adding a small sign hoping residents would not leave windows open.

Public footways under facades, opening lights, curtain walling, hoardings, catch fans and demolition protection are temporary works items while the building is being built, altered or left in a temporary condition. CDM 2015 duties to people other than employees sit alongside the project temporary works procedure. BS 5975-1:2024 puts falling-object and public-interface items on the register, names a TWC, requires a brief when the opening direction, restraint or exclusion zone changes, and requires inspection after a near-miss. A review that is not closed out is not control. A sign on the glass is not a restraint. Wind does not have to be exceptional to generate a falling unit.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Register facade opening lights, curtain walling, catch fans, hoardings and any unit that can fall onto a public route.
If the opening direction changes from inward to outward, treat that as a new design brief, not a product tweak.
Do not accept a single unproven restrictor as the only load path over a live pavement.
Obtain manufacturer confirmation that fittings suit the actual geometry, including curved or bespoke units.
A near-miss during construction is a hold point: stop, redesign, inspect, permit before the public walks back underneath.
Close out review actions in writing. A slide deck is not evidence.
Provisional category only — confirm under the project temporary works procedure. Public interface and high consequence push the category up.
Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.
